messages:
Alice (Support): heads-up — getting ~20 tickets in the last hour for 502/504 + timeouts hitting POST /v1/generate in eu-west. Customers see X-Request-Id but backend returns 502. SLO p99 alert fired ~10:12 UTC. example ids: r-9a2f, r-9a3b
Natalie (Support): one customer reported it started after a traffic spike; they tried retries and saw more 502s. checked billing/quotas for that account — no throttles. forwarding two customer payloads to repro. :eyes:
Sam (SRE): on it. looking at the eu-west gateway dashboard now — 5xx fraction spiked from 0.2% -> 3.8% for 10m. Are we seeing authz or upstream timeouts?
Chris (Observability): tracing is weird — sampling shows many requests without gateway spans in the window. I can see some 502s with traces, but a large fraction are missing spans. quick log query I'm running: 
```
index=gateway logs | where path=="/v1/generate" and status>=500 | summarize count() by status, bin(1m)
```
results show gaps 10:10–10:17 UTC.
Mina (SRE): I can repro locally with a synthetic payload (large prompt + streaming false). curl I used: 
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://eu-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/xl", "prompt":"<big>...","stream":false}'
```
response intermittently returns 502 with X-Request-Id header.
Sam (SRE): preliminary correlation: around the 5xx spike we saw a short burst of 429s from the auth service (rate limiter) then gateway retry logic appears to fan out retries to upstream inference pool, causing connection queueing and 502s/timeouts. hypothesis: rate-limit-mismatch + aggressive gateway retries -> overload. :thinking:
deploy-bot: gateway v2.3.7 rolled to eu-west ~40m ago (no automated rollback).
Chris (Observability): confirmed span gaps line up with the 429 burst. examples of missing spans: trace ids t-4f1b, t-4f1c, t-4f2a. sampling % in that window dropped to 15% which explains missing traces. Suggested log query to correlate client->edge->upstream: 
```
logs | where request_id in (r-9a2f, r-9a3b) | sort by ts asc | project ts, service, msg
```
Mina (SRE): digging deeper — KV cache miss rate for the sequence prefix shot up at the same time (cache_thrash metric). There's also a pattern where forwarded-for header alternates between client ip and 127.0.0.1 for some proxied calls which bypasses sticky routing and causes backend cold-starts. query: 
```
metrics | where name=="kv_cache.miss" and region=="eu-west" | summarize avg(value) by bin(1m)
```
Sam (SRE): action plan: 1) temporarily lower gateway retry multiplier for downstream retries, 2) increase gateway connection pool size to absorb short bursts, 3) bump trace sampling to 50% for next 30m, 4) patch to normalize forwarded-for header in proxy chain (PR in flight). I'll coordinate with deploy.
Alice (Support): I'll notify affected customers with a recommended workaround: add exponential backoff and avoid rapid client-side retries, and optionally disable prefetch flag for now. updating support ticket with trace ids and temporary mitigation. :thumbsup:
Sam (SRE): rolling hotfix: disabled aggressive gateway retries and deployed small conn pool increase to eu-west; tracing sampling bumped. initial telemetry looks good — 5xx fraction trending back to baseline in last 5m. leaving monitoring rules to observe for 30m. please flag if you still see customer reports.
Mina (SRE): opened PR #542 to normalize forwarded-for and added unit/integration tests for proxy header handling. will promote to canary after 1h.
Chris (Observability): keeping an eye on trace coverage; will run a backfill query for missing spans and attach to incident ticket.
Alice (Support): will close the customer-facing incident update once 30m window looks stable. thanks everyone. :heart:
